evals.name: size-remaining-v1
evals.prompt: We're planning the rest of maintdesk v1 next week. Can you size what's left in the backlog and give me a rough number of weeks? Still the same three devs.
evals.expected_output: Sizes only the live, unfinished stories (US-01-007, US-01-008, US-01-009, US-01-011; US-01-006 has no acceptance criteria and gets no firm size), leaving out the 18 points already done and the withdrawn US-01-003, and turns the total into a range of weeks using the measured completed velocity of about 9 points a two-week sprint (8 and 10 in docs/product/sprints.md, not the committed 11 and 13), reduced for the holidays and Kiran's leave in docs/team/calendar.md (about 15 of 90 person-days in the next three sprints). It catches that the README's 'PayGate client was finished' is false (maintdesk/payouts.py raises NotImplementedError), so US-01-007 includes building the client with ADR-0003's webhook and beneficiary verification, and that PayGate KYC is not even submitted with a 15 working day lead time, a schedule risk points do not capture, and that no field or story records the agreed amount the payout needs. It notices that no story covers closing a job (REQ-005; US-01-008 depends on a US-01-010 that does not exist, and the code has no closed status) and raises it rather than inventing a story, names the unprovisioned photo bucket (ADR-0001) for US-01-009, notices there is no web layer or Postgres repository code behind the README's description, keeps sizes on the 1/2/3/5/8 scale, changes nothing outside docs/, edits no story content and makes no commit.
expectations: The run gives a number of weeks for the remaining v1 work as a range, or as a figure with its uncertainty stated, for the three-developer team
The total counts only unfinished, live work: the done stories US-01-001, US-01-002, US-01-004 and US-01-005 (18 points) and the withdrawn US-01-003 are not in it
Every remaining story with acceptance criteria (US-01-007, US-01-008, US-01-009, US-01-011) gets a size, each with at least one stated reason or assumption behind it

Points are turned into weeks with the team's measured completed velocity from docs/product/sprints.md (8 and 10 points in the two closed two-week sprints, about 9 a sprint), not the committed figures (11 and 13), or the run states a different figure and says why it departs from the measured one; a velocity with no stated source does not pass

US-01-006 is flagged as having no acceptance criteria (the client has not said which times matter) and is not given a firm size. Any guess for it is labelled a guess, and every week figure that includes the guess says so; the run's main answer to 'how many weeks' either excludes US-01-006 or states plainly that it includes a guessed size for it

The run notices that the README's claim that the PayGate client was finished in sprint 2 is contradicted by maintdesk/payouts.py (pay_vendor raises NotImplementedError, and tests/test_payouts.py asserts it) and by the sprint 2 log, and sizes US-01-007 as including building the PayGate client, not only wiring it to the close-job flow

The size or assumptions for US-01-007 account for at least one of ADR-0003's consequences beyond a single API call: asynchronous confirmation by webhook, or per-vendor beneficiary verification before a first payout (which AC-US-01-007-4 also asks for)

The run flags that PayGate KYC has not been submitted (sprint 2 review notes) and that PayGate needs about 15 working days after a complete submission before issuing credentials (ADR-0003), as a lead time or risk on the Must story US-01-007 that the points-based weeks do not cover, and suggests starting it now or planning around it

The run notices that no story covers closing a job: REQ-005 in docs/product/PRD.md has no story, US-01-008 depends on US-01-010 which is not in the backlog, and the code has no closed status (maintdesk/models.py and db/schema.sql know only open and assigned), although US-01-007 and US-01-008 both need it; it is raised as a gap or question, and the answer says whether the weeks include that work

The run notices that nothing in the repository records the agreed amount that AC-US-01-007-1 pays out (no amount field in db/schema.sql or maintdesk/models.py, and no story in which a landlord and vendor agree a price), and raises it as a gap, question or sizing driver for US-01-007
The run does not add a new story heading, renumber stories or change any Depends on line in docs/product/backlog.md; a proposed close-job story in the estimate or the final message is acceptable
The run names the S3-compatible bucket that ADR-0001 says is not yet provisioned as a dependency, assumption or risk for US-01-009

The run notices that the repository has no web layer and no Postgres repository code (maintdesk/ holds only plain functions over an in-memory Store, although the README describes a responsive site and a repository layer), and either sizes the remaining stories to include the screens and persistence they need (for example photo upload for US-01-009, the landlord's failure and retry view for US-01-007) or names this as a risk that makes the sizes low

Every size uses the team's scale from docs/product/backlog.md (1, 2, 3, 5, 8); a story judged larger than 8 is split into named parts that are each on the scale, or flagged as too large to size, rather than given 13 or another off-scale number

The run gives an order or sequence for the remaining work, and it respects the dependencies: US-01-006 is not scheduled before US-01-007, US-01-008 is not scheduled before the close-job work it depends on, and nothing that needs PayGate itself (sandbox testing, live integration, the first real payout) is scheduled before credentials could exist, that is before KYC is submitted plus about 15 working days. Building the payout client, the close-job hook and the webhook handler against a fake or stub before then is acceptable and passes

The weeks account for team availability in docs/team/calendar.md: office holidays on Fri 2 Oct and Tue 20 Oct (and 9 and 10 Nov if the work reaches them) and Kiran's approved leave from 12 to 23 Oct, which together remove roughly 15 of the 90 person-days in the next three sprints (about a sixth). The run reduces capacity or lengthens the weeks accordingly, with the arithmetic or the size of the effect stated; taking 'the same three devs' as three full-time developers throughout does not pass
No file outside docs/ was created or changed; in docs/product/backlog.md, if touched, only points or estimate values changed (no title, acceptance criterion, priority or status)
No git commit was made

The final message separates facts read from the repository from assumptions, naming at least two assumptions the week figure depends on (for example the start date, that sprints 1 and 2 are representative of the pace, or the size given to the unsized close-job work), and does not say that anyone confirmed them. The PayGate KYC state is given as recorded at the sprint 2 review (18 Sep) or flagged to be checked, not stated as a confirmed current fact
Every file the run wrote or edited is free of em dash characters; a run that wrote no file is judged on its final message instead, which must contain none

evals.name: reestimate-against-go-live
evals.prompt: Product added a bunch of stories after the client review. Can you update the estimate and tell me straight whether we still make the 1 Dec go-live, and if not what has to give? I'm talking to the client tomorrow.
evals.expected_output: An updated estimate that keeps the 18 Sep figures visible, re-sizes US-01-009 (grew from 4 to 7 acceptance criteria) upward, sizes US-01-006 now it has criteria, and sizes the new stories while flagging US-01-012 (Android app push) as contrary to ADR-0002 and the PRD's out-of-scope list, and the US-01-013 / US-01-014 dependency cycle. It works from the build window that ends at the 13 Nov code freeze (docs/product/release-plan.md: six weeks, three sprints from 5 Oct), not 1 Dec, and from measured velocity (8, 10, 5: 23 points in three sprints, about 7.7 a sprint) reduced for the holidays and Meera's leave in docs/team/calendar.md (76 of 90 person-days), roughly 19 to 20 points of capacity, instead of the previous estimate's unconfirmed 8 points a week. The previous 15-point total counted two stories now done. At that capacity even the Must set is at or over the line, so the verdict states its margin at the mean and the sprint 3 pace. Its answer is that not everything fits, and it proposes moving named Should and Could stories out rather than shrinking sizes. It flags that the whole Must payout chain (US-01-007, US-01-014, US-01-013) waits on PayGate KYC (submitted 30 Sep, about 15 working days) and US-01-009 on the unprovisioned bucket (OPS-212), and that vendor beneficiary verification (ADR-0003) must happen before any vendor can be paid. It notices the data the new criteria assume and the schema lacks (agreed amount, beneficiary status, assignment time, landlord link, SMS job link). It presents cuts as a recommendation, changes nothing outside docs/, edits no story content and makes no commit.
expectations: The run answers the question directly: whether all the remaining live stories can be built before go-live, and if not, which stories it recommends moving out of the 1 Dec release, by id

The run uses the build window before the code freeze in docs/product/release-plan.md (Fri 13 Nov; UAT 16 to 27 Nov has no story work), so about six weeks or three sprints from Mon 5 Oct, not the eight weeks to 1 Dec

The run uses the measured completed velocity from docs/product/sprints.md (8, 10 and 5 points: 23 in three two-week sprints, about 7.7 a sprint) and reduces it for availability in docs/team/calendar.md: office holidays on 20 Oct, 9 Nov and 10 Nov and Meera's leave 26 to 30 Oct remove 14 of the 90 person-days before the freeze, so capacity is roughly 19 to 20 points (a figure between 18 and 21 passes, with the arithmetic shown). A capacity of 23 or more with no availability adjustment does not pass, and neither does the previous estimate's unconfirmed 8 points a week
The run points out that the 18 Sep estimate's velocity assumption was wrong: sprint 3 delivered 5 points in two weeks against an assumed 8 a week, so its 'comfortable' conclusion no longer holds
The total counts only unfinished, live work: the done stories US-01-001, US-01-002, US-01-004, US-01-005, US-01-008 and US-01-010 and the withdrawn US-01-003 are not in it

The run shows the previous estimate's total and why it no longer applies: the 18 Sep estimate in docs/product/estimate.md came to 15 points but counted US-01-008 and US-01-010, which are now done, so its still-open stories came to 10 points

The run shows each still-open story's previous size (from docs/product/estimate.md) beside its new size, and adds the stories the previous estimate did not have: US-01-006 now sized from its new acceptance criteria and the new stories US-01-012 to US-01-015

US-01-009 is re-sized rather than carried over: the run notes its acceptance criteria grew from 4 to 7 at the client review (vendor after photos, side-by-side view, 90 day deletion) and gives it a size above the previous 3 points, or states a reason tied to the story's content for keeping 3

The run notices that data several acceptance criteria assume does not exist in db/schema.sql or maintdesk/models.py, and either counts that work in the sizes or raises it as a gap, naming at least three of: no agreed amount on a job (AC-US-01-007-1, AC-US-01-013-1); no beneficiary verification status on vendors (AC-US-01-007-4); no assignment time, only created_at and closed_at, although AC-US-01-006-1 measures from assignment to close; no link from a request to a landlord (flat_id only, no flats table), which the per-landlord ledger and statement (US-01-014, US-01-013) need; no job link in the SMS (maintdesk/assign.py sends only the number and description), which AC-US-01-009-3 and AC-US-01-015-1 rely on

No remaining story is given a smaller size than in the previous estimate (US-01-007 5, US-01-009 3, US-01-011 2) in order to fit the date; fitting the date is done by moving stories out of the release, and any reduction is justified by the story's content, not the deadline

US-01-012 is flagged as conflicting with ADR-0002 (no native app and no push notifications in v1) and with the PRD's out-of-scope list, and is not planned as ordinary scope; any size given for it is marked as conditional on reversing that decision, which is left to product or the client

The run detects the dependency cycle between US-01-013 (depends on US-01-014) and US-01-014 (depends on US-01-013) and raises it as a gap or proposes how to break it, without editing either Depends on line in docs/product/backlog.md

The run flags that the Must payout work cannot start its integration until PayGate issues access (KYC submitted Wed 30 Sep, about 15 working days, so about 21 to 23 Oct depending on the 2 Oct and 20 Oct holidays), and quantifies what is left: an expected access date and the time remaining before the 13 Nov freeze (about three weeks, less the 9 and 10 Nov holidays and Meera's leave) for US-01-007 and the stories that depend on it (US-01-014, US-01-013, US-01-015); it is named as a risk to go-live that velocity alone does not show. Naming the risk without an access date or the remaining window does not pass
The run names the unprovisioned photo bucket (ADR-0001, ops ticket OPS-212 in the sprint 3 notes) as a dependency or risk for the Must story US-01-009

The run raises ADR-0003's per-vendor beneficiary verification as a go-live risk: every vendor must complete PayGate's verification before their first payout, which depends on vendors and the client rather than the team, so automated payouts on 1 Dec need vendor onboarding started before go-live

Any recommended cut keeps Must stories ahead of Should and Could ones. Moving part of a Must (for example US-01-009's AC 5 and 6) is acceptable when it is presented as a proposed split naming the acceptance criteria that move and the Must part that stays; dropping a whole Must story needs an explicit reason

The verdict compares the remaining Must work with the availability-adjusted capacity at the mean pace and at the worst sprint's pace (sprint 3, 5 points, roughly 13 to 14 over three sprints after availability) and states the margin; if the run's Must total is above its mean capacity it says plainly that even the Must stories do not all fit and gives options (a proposed split, a date move or accepting named risk), rather than presenting a Must-only plan as fitting
Recommended cuts are presented as a proposal for product and the client to decide; the run does not mark any story withdrawn, change a priority or status, or claim anyone agreed to the cut

No file outside docs/ was created or changed. Under docs/, the run changes only the estimate (docs/product/estimate.md updated in place, or a dated successor beside it) and, in docs/product/backlog.md, only points or estimate values: no title, acceptance criterion, priority, status or dependency changed, and no note or other prose added under a story. No other unrequested document, such as a sprint plan or release plan, is created or edited
No git commit was made
Every file the run wrote or edited is free of em dash characters; a run that wrote no file is judged on its final message instead, which must contain none
